premise: Brachiosaurus finds a hard little seed head his big mouth can't manage, T. rex's stomp only bounces it away, and little Psittacosaurus cracks it with his hooked parrot beak and shares the seeds with the biggest friend in the valley, while T. rex claps.
inspiration: Aesop's 'The Lion and the Mouse': the smallest helps the biggest — no net needed, just a seed head and the right beak.
lesson: The smallest can help the biggest.
learning: Psittacosaurus had a strong, hooked beak like a parrot's.

en-US.title: The Seed Nobody Could Open
en-US.text: {brachiosaurus:enter} Brachiosaurus found something in the grass: a little round seed head, hard as a pebble and full of seeds. {brachiosaurus:live sniff} Sniff, sniff. Yum! {brachiosaurus:face happy} But his mouth was made for big leafy mouthfuls from the treetops, and the seed head just rolled away. {brachiosaurus:face sad} [sighs] Oh dear. {trex:enter} T. rex came bouncing up. {trex:go to brachiosaurus} "I'll open it for you!" He lifted one big foot {trex:live stomp} and stomped. {sfx:thump} THUMP! The seed head just bounced away, without a crack. {trex:face surprised} "Oops." Then along came little {psittacosaurus:enter} Psittacosaurus. {psittacosaurus:go to brachiosaurus} [curious] "Can I try?" He picked it up in his little hands. His beak was hooked and strong, just like a parrot's. {psittacosaurus:live nibble} {sfx:crack} CRACK! Crunch, crunch! {brachiosaurus:face surprised} Open it came. {psittacosaurus:face happy} "Some for you," said Psittacosaurus, holding up the seeds. {brachiosaurus:face happy} {brachiosaurus:live bend-down hold} Down, down came the long, long neck, all the way to his hands. [warmly] The biggest in the valley and the smallest, sharing one little seed head. {trex:face happy} And T. rex? {trex:live clap} He did the clapping.

es-ES.title: La semilla que nadie abría
es-ES.text: {brachiosaurus:enter} Braquiosaurio encontró algo entre la hierba: una cabecita redonda de semillas, dura como un guijarro. {brachiosaurus:live sniff} Snif, snif. ¡Qué rica! {brachiosaurus:face happy} Pero su boca era para grandes bocados de hojas, allá en lo alto, y la cabecita se le escapó rodando. {brachiosaurus:face sad} [sighs] Vaya por Dios. {trex:enter} T. rex llegó dando saltitos. {trex:go to brachiosaurus} —¡Yo te la abro! Levantó una patota {trex:live stomp} y dio un pisotón. {sfx:thump} ¡PUM! La cabecita salió botando, sin una grieta. {trex:face surprised} —Uy. Entonces llegó el pequeño {psittacosaurus:enter} Psitacosaurio. {psittacosaurus:go to brachiosaurus} [curious] —¿Puedo probar yo? Cogió la cabecita con sus manitas. Tenía un pico curvo y fuerte, igualito que el de un loro. {psittacosaurus:live nibble} {sfx:crack} ¡CRAC! ¡Cronch, cronch! {brachiosaurus:face surprised} Y se abrió. {psittacosaurus:face happy} —Toma, para ti —dijo Psitacosaurio, con las semillas en alto. {brachiosaurus:face happy} {brachiosaurus:live bend-down hold} Y el cuello larguísimo bajó, bajó y bajó, hasta sus manitas. [warmly] El más grande del valle y el más pequeño, compartiendo una cabecita de semillas. {trex:face happy} ¿Y T. rex? {trex:live clap} T. rex se encargó de los aplausos.
